messages.text: Van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Van Veen makes history

metadata.summary: Dutch favourite Michael van Gerwen suffered a shock second-round exit at the Dutch Darts Championship on Saturday, losing 6-5 to Irishman William O'Connor.
metadata.content: Dutch Darts Championship: Michael van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Gian van Veen makes history and Gerwyn Price triumphs on return | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Dutch Darts Championship: Michael van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Gian van Veen makes history and Gerwyn Price triumphs on return Michael van Gerwen's poor form in 2026 continues as he suffers second-round Dutch Darts Championship defeat to Williams O'Connor; Gerwyn Price, Gian van Veen, Stephen Bunting, Nathan Aspinall each progress; watch Grand Slam of Darts live on Sky Sports from November 14-22 Sunday 18 October 2026 01:06, UK Image: Michael van Gerwen suffered another early tournament exit in 2026 at the Dutch Darts Championship Dutch favourite Michael van Gerwen suffered a shock second-round exit at the Dutch Darts Championship on Saturday, losing 6-5 to Irishman William O'Connor. The defeat extends Van Gerwen's poor run of form, having lost his opening match at four European Tour events this season before arriving in Maastricht: the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix, Flanders Darts Trophy and Swiss Darts Trophy. It marks his most first-round exits in a single season since the tour began in 2012. O'Connor produced a superb display, firing in three ton-plus checkouts of 136, 131 and 121 to seal his victory and book his place in round three. Liverpool spent close to £400m on Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. Against Brentford, there was evidence that expensively-assembled attack might finally be clicking. Isak was on the fringes of the game for long periods, limited to only 16 touches by the dogged hosts. But his brilliantly-taken goal, controlled and rifled home with dizzying speed in the second half, was a reminder of just how deadly he can be at his best. It took him to five goals for the season. Only Erling Haaland has scored more in the Premier League. He is putting a difficult first season behind him and Andoni Iraola will be encouraged that it was Barcola who provided the assist. metadata.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets."
metadata.content: Sonay Kartal on 'dream come true' Wuhan Open run as British player reaches first WTA 1000 final | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sonay Kartal on 'dream come true' Wuhan Open run as British player reaches first WTA 1000 final Great Britain's Sonay Kartal says mental side of sport "one of my strongest assets" as she prepares for Wuhan Open final against Poland's Maja Chwalinska on Sunday, live on Sky Sports Tennis from 11.30am ; Kartal beat Jelena Ostapenko 7-6 7-6 in semi-finals on Saturday Saturday 17 October 2026 18:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open semi-final between Sonay Kartal and Jelena Ostapenko Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets." Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Jelena Ostapenko. The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match. messages.text: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes

metadata.summary: Ombudsman exacted Qatar Racing Champion Stakes revenge on Calandagan to come out on top with a show-stopping performance at Ascot.
metadata.content: Ascot: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes for Gosden team | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ascot: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes for Gosden team Ombudsman reversed the form with last year's winner Calandagan in the latest renewal of the Qatar Racing Champion Stakes at Ascot under William Buick; result was one of three successes on the day for owners Godolphin, who also claimed the QEII and Balmoral Handicap Saturday 17 October 2026 17:06, UK Image: Ombudsman won the Champion Stakes Ombudsman exacted Qatar Racing Champion Stakes revenge on Calandagan to come out on top with a show-stopping performance at Ascot. It was Francis-Henri Graffard's French raider who took home the spoils 12 months ago, but this time around there was a decisive verdict in favour of John and Thady Gosden's home favourite, who obliged as the 5-4 market leader. With the six-strong field heading into the home straight grouped tightly, the stage was set for Ombudsman to demonstrate the blistering turn of foot that has often been a hallmark of his career. When William Buick asked him to quicken, he scorched past eventual third Bay City Roller before seeing off Calandagan to banish Juddmonte International disappointment and prove he is truly one of the best middle-distance horses on the planet.
